title: DCGS-A support, evaluation, performance, substitution, and exit join · acquisition 01

selection_contract.universe: The bounded DCGS-A Increment 2 and Capability Drop chronology already frozen by SSC-F13-DCGSA-01.

sources.title: Army releases DCGS-A Increment 2 request for proposals
supports: The Army described a market-research process and a full-and-open competition objective.
The announcement establishes the acquisition claim but not the complete contacted-vendor, proposal, support, evaluation or performance denominator.

sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc., B-412746
supports: Palantir challenged the earlier integrated acquisition approach.
GAO denied the protest on the record before it.
The record preserved commercial, government, open-source, phased and integrated alternatives rather than a Palantir-only universe.
does_not_support: a complete or fair option set

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc. v. United States, No. 17-1465
supports: The Court of Federal Claims enjoined the earlier solicitation for noncompliance with commercial-item market-research requirements.
The Federal Circuit affirmed the injunction.
An external correction route altered the challenged acquisition.
does_not_support: fairness of every later option set

sources.title: General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc., B-416181
supports: The later Capability Drop 1 procurement received eight proposals.
The public decision names General Dynamics, Raytheon and Palantir; five offeror identities remain unrecovered in the public record used here.
Offerors performed a live product demonstration covering 32 tasks within an approximately 70-requirement technical framework.

The public evaluation table rated Raytheon Good, Palantir Acceptable and General Dynamics Unacceptable, with evaluated prices of approximately 305.4 million, 349.3 million and 202.2 million dollars respectively.
The Army awarded multiple IDIQ contracts to Raytheon and Palantir, and GAO denied General Dynamics' technical-evaluation protest.
does_not_support: the identities or dispositions of all eight offerors
equal pre-demonstration data, assistance or test access
technical superiority beyond the bounded evaluation

sources.title: Under secretary sees strength of Army intelligence capabilities firsthand in Fort Hood visit
supports: The Army conducted a 2018 operational test of Capability Drop 1 with intelligence soldiers and multiple Army and DoD test partners.
The test was designed to inform suitability, survivability, effectiveness and mission-effect evaluation.

sources.publisher: U.S. Army Capability Program Executive, Intelligence and Spectrum Warfare
sources.title: PM Intelligence Systems and Analytics portfolio
supports: The Army describes Capability Drop 1 as a current tactical battalion toolset.
The page reports 879 CD1 systems fielded to 402 maneuver battalions as of FY2021.
The page identifies continuing fielding, workstation refresh and interface work, and identifies Army Intelligence Data Platform as formerly DCGS-A CD-2.
does_not_support: complete replacement, substitution or exit history

sources.title: Palantir delivery order W56KGY25F0153
supports: A 2025 delivery order to Palantir supported the Intelligence Systems and Analytics Capability Drop 1 capability through a Hydra engineering change proposal.
The award records continuing modification or support after the original fielding period.

sources.title: Palantir delivery order W56KGY25F0105
supports: A 2025 Palantir delivery order supported Capability Drop 2 through data integrations and exercise support.
The order shows continued Palantir work within the broader intelligence portfolio.
